title.es: Seguir un debate a dos voces

es: Seguir un debate breve y construir un mapa con argumento, contraargumento, concesión y cierre.

teaching.en: The moderator reads the motion aloud and gives each speaker two minutes, then reminds the audience to weigh up the arguments before voting.
teaching.es: La moderadora lee la moción en voz alta y da dos minutos a cada orador; luego recuerda al público que sopese los argumentos antes de votar.
teaching.explanationEs: El moderador dirige el debate; la moción es la frase que se discute; weigh up = sopesar.
segments: The moderator reads the motion aloud and gives each speaker two minutes,
then reminds the audience to weigh up the arguments before voting.
teaching.audioText: The moderator reads the motion aloud and gives each speaker two minutes, then reminds the audience to weigh up the arguments before voting.

teaching.en: The motion is that mobile phones should be banned in class, and Tom is in favour of it, although his stance is more nuanced than it sounds.
teaching.es: La moción es que se prohíban los teléfonos celulares en clase, y Tom está a favor, aunque su postura es más matizada de lo que parece.
teaching.explanationEs: In favour of = a favor de; stance es la postura que alguien defiende.
segments: The motion is that mobile phones should be banned in class, and Tom is
in favour of it, although his stance is more nuanced than it sounds.
teaching.audioText: The motion is that mobile phones should be banned in class, and Tom is in favour of it, although his stance is more nuanced than it sounds.

teaching.en: Ana is against the motion, and her main contention is that phones are useful tools, provided that teachers set clear limits.
teaching.es: Ana está en contra de la moción y su tesis principal es que los teléfonos son herramientas útiles, siempre que los profesores pongan límites claros.
teaching.explanationEs: Against va sin preposición detrás: against the motion; contention es la tesis que alguien defiende con sus razones.
segments: Ana is against the motion, and her main contention is that
phones are useful tools, provided that teachers set clear limits.
teaching.audioText: Ana is against the motion, and her main contention is that phones are useful tools, provided that teachers set clear limits.

teaching.en: Tom's counterargument is that the premise behind Ana's case, that students use phones only for study, is simply unrealistic.
teaching.es: El contraargumento de Tom es que la premisa del caso de Ana, que los estudiantes usan el teléfono solo para estudiar, es sencillamente poco realista.
teaching.explanationEs: El contraargumento responde a lo que dijo el otro orador; la premisa es la idea que se da por supuesta.
segments: Tom's counterargument is that the premise behind Ana's case, that
students use phones only for study, is simply unrealistic.
teaching.audioText: Tom's counterargument is that the premise behind Ana's case, that students use phones only for study, is simply unrealistic.

teaching.en: Both speakers eventually find some common ground, yet each expects the other to carry the burden of proof, and their closing statements still differ on whether a total ban is necessary.
teaching.es: Ambos oradores acaban encontrando cierto terreno común, pero cada uno espera que el otro cargue con la carga de la prueba, y sus declaraciones de cierre siguen difiriendo sobre si hace falta una prohibición total.
teaching.explanationEs: Common ground = lo que ambos aceptan; burden of proof = quién debe demostrar su tesis; closing statement: la frase final donde cada orador resume su postura.
segments: Both speakers eventually find some common ground, yet each expects the other to carry the burden
of proof, and their closing statements still differ on whether a total ban is necessary.

teaching.en: To sum up, the debate shows that the motion divides the class, and a good moderator records each argument fairly.
teaching.es: En resumen, el debate demuestra que la moción divide a la clase, y un buen moderador recoge cada argumento con justicia.
teaching.explanationEs: To sum up abre el resumen final; es la señal del cierre.
segments: To sum up, the debate shows that the motion divides
the class, and a good moderator records each argument fairly.

prompt.es: Lee la intervención. ¿Qué papel cumple dentro del mapa del debate?

choices.text: It answers what the previous speaker claimed.
It states her position and gives one reason for it.
It summarises both sides at the end of the debate.

feedback.es: Ana toma postura (against the motion) y da una razón: es un argumento, no una respuesta ni un cierre.

hint.es: Comprueba si la frase toma postura y aporta una razón.

origin.text: Ana is against the motion. Her argument is that phones help students look up information quickly and organise their homework.

prompt.es: Completa: «Ana habla en contra de la moción, porque cree que los teléfonos son útiles.»

feedback.es: Against va sin preposición detrás: Ana habla en contra de la moción (against it).

hint.es: Es lo contrario de in favour of y no lleva preposición detrás.

origin.text: The moderator has read the motion. Ana speaks ___ it, because she believes that phones are useful tools for students.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En resumen, la moción divide a la clase.»

answer.text: To sum up, the motion divides the class

feedback.es: To sum up abre el cierre del debate y resume la situación final.

hint.es: Empieza por la fórmula que introduce el resumen.

prompt.es: Escucha el resumen del debate y elige cuál es el contraargumento de Ana.

choices.text: That notifications harm the concentration of students.
That some students use their phones badly in class.
That phones give students quick access to useful tools.

feedback.es: El contraargumento de Ana es que los teléfonos dan acceso inmediato a herramientas útiles; las otras dos ideas son el argumento de Tom y la concesión de Ana.

origin.audio: The moderator opened the debate on whether phones should be banned in class. Tom spoke in favour of the motion: his main argument was that notifications harm concentration. Ana, who was against it, offered a counterargument: phones give students quick access to dictionaries and calendars, and banning them would only hide their use. Granted, she said, some students use them badly. Even so, she preferred clear rules to a total ban. Tom replied that the premise of her case, that students can control themselves, was unrealistic.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué premisa discute Tom.

choices.text: That students can control their own phone use.
That phones are useful for dictionaries and calendars.
That a total ban would be easy to apply in class.

feedback.es: Tom discute la premisa de que los estudiantes saben controlarse: para él, eso es poco realista.

Granted, she said, some students use them badly. Even so, she preferred clear rules to a total ban. Tom replied that the premise of her case, that students can control themselves, was unrealistic.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su pieza en el mapa del debate.

pairs: My main argument is that phones distract.

pairs.es: Planteas tu postura y su razón

pairs: On the other hand, phones also help students.

pairs.es: Respondes a lo que dijo el otro lado

pairs: Granted, some students use them badly.

pairs.es: Admites un punto del otro lado

pairs: To sum up, the class remains divided.

feedback.es: Cada pieza del mapa tiene su palabra señal: argumento, contraargumento, concesión y cierre.

prompt.es: Escucha el cierre y elige qué concede Tom en su declaración final.

choices.text: That phones are useful tools for students in class.
That a total ban would be hard to apply.
That clear rules alone would solve the whole problem.

feedback.es: Tom concede que una prohibición es difícil de aplicar; los otros dos puntos son de Ana.

origin.audio: In the second half, the moderator asked each speaker for a closing statement. Ana admitted that phones are a distraction, but she insisted that rules, not bans, solve the problem. Tom admitted that a ban is hard to apply, yet he insisted that those who want phones in class must prove that they help.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué postura adopta Tom sobre quién debe probar su caso.

choices.text: He thinks that those who want a ban must prove that it works.
He wants the school to test the ban before voting.
He expects those who favour phones to show real benefits.

feedback.es: Tom insiste en que quienes quieren los teléfonos en clase deben demostrar que ayudan: les traslada la carga de la prueba.

origin.audio: In the second half, the moderator asked each speaker for a closing statement. Ana admitted that phones are a distraction, but she insisted that rules, not bans, solve the problem. Tom admitted that a ban is hard to apply, yet he insisted that those who want phones in class must prove that they help.

prompt.es: Completa: «Sin un ganador claro, la moderadora pidió buscar un terreno común.»

feedback.es: Common ground es lo que ambas partes aceptan, aunque sigan discrepando en otros puntos.

origin.text: With no clear winner, the moderator asked both teams to look for common ___ before the vote.

prompt.es: Lee la intervención. ¿Qué postura y qué premisa refleja Ana?

choices.text: She is against a ban, and assumes that students can learn to control themselves.
She is against a ban, and assumes that teachers will check it very strictly.
She is in favour of a ban, and assumes that students cannot ever learn.

feedback.es: Prefiere enseñar a gestionar los teléfonos en lugar de prohibirlos: está en contra y da por supuesto que los estudiantes pueden aprender a controlarse.

origin.text: Ana said: 'I would rather teach students to manage their phones than pretend the phones do not exist. A ban only hides the problem, and a hidden problem is exactly where teachers cannot help.'

prompt.es: Lee la nota. ¿Por qué salió derrotada la moción?

choices.text: Tom failed to give a closing statement before the vote.
Ana's flexible proposal persuaded several listeners who had not decided.
The audience wanted the class to keep using phones all day.

feedback.es: La propuesta flexible de Ana, con normas limitadas, convenció a los indecisos aunque el argumento de Tom era sólido.

origin.text: Final note from the moderator: the motion was narrowly defeated. Although Tom's argument about concentration was strong, Ana's counterargument about quick access carried more weight with the audience, and her closing statement, offering limited rules, won over several listeners who had not decided.

prompt.es: Completa: «Con dos casos igual de sólidos, los jueces tuvieron que sopesar las pruebas.»

feedback.es: Weigh up significa sopesar: comparar con cuidado las pruebas de cada lado antes de decidir.

origin.text: With two equally strong cases, the judges had to ___ up the evidence carefully before announcing the result.

prompt.es: Escucha el comentario y elige qué valoró la estudiante del debate.

choices.text: That one of the speakers had much better evidence than the other.
That the moderator forced both sides to reach an agreement.
That the speakers fairly acknowledged each other's strongest points.

feedback.es: Lo que le hizo cambiar de opinión fue que ambos reconocieron los mejores puntos del otro antes de replicar.

origin.audio: After the vote, a student said she had arrived in favour of the ban and left against it. It was not a single argument that changed her mind, she explained, but the way both speakers accepted each other's best points before replying.
